Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: A friend on their way to the airport calls, thinking they left their passport at home, and asks if you can check and bring it to them right away.
Situation2: They organize an intensive workshop for community leaders to deeply understand and apply complex theological concepts.
Story: I was reviewing my notes for the workshop, heart pounding with anticipation. Today’s session was crucial—community leaders were counting on me to guide them through some of the most challenging theological concepts. I’d spent weeks preparing, and I knew how much they expected from me, not just as a teacher, but as a spiritual guide. Just as I was about to leave for the church, my phone buzzed. It was Mark, my oldest friend, his voice frantic. He was on his way to the airport and thought he’d left his passport at home. “Can you check and bring it to me? I’ll miss my flight otherwise,” he pleaded. I glanced at the clock. If I left now, I’d barely make it back in time for the workshop, if at all. My mind raced—Mark had always been there for me, and I knew he was counting on me now. But the church was expecting me, too, and I couldn’t let them down. The weight of both roles pressed on me, each demanding my presence, each impossible to ignore.
